International organic revenue growth accelerated to 8%, the strongest rate since Q1 2024, suggesting the global business is gaining momentum. The full-year revenue guide was largely reiterated at plus 3%, providing some top-line stability.

Core operating margins contracted 35 basis points year over year in Q3 as cost increases and higher advertising spending overwhelmed productivity savings and tariff refunds. North America beverages and international beverages both missed expectations, and management acknowledged the domestic business performed below expectations.

However, the full-year core EPS growth outlook was cut to approximately 3% at the midpoint from roughly 5% due to North America margin pressure, with core operating margins contracting 35 basis points year over year. tts_summary: Here's what you need to know from this morning's Pepsi earnings note. This is a single-stock release with no broad macro commentary, so let's get right into it. Pepsi posted third-quarter earnings per share of two dollars and thirty-four cents, beating the Street's estimate of two twenty-nine by about two percent. Organic sales grew three point one percent, the fastest rate since the fourth quarter of twenty twenty-three, and that topped the consensus estimate of two point six five percent. On the surface, those are solid numbers. But here's the catch — the company cut its full-year core earnings per share growth outlook to roughly three percent at the midpoint, down from the prior guide of approximately five percent. That reduction is being driven entirely by margin pressure in North America, where operating cost increases and higher advertising and marketing spending overwhelmed productivity savings, price hikes, and tariff refunds. Core operating margins contracted thirty-five basis points year over year in the quarter. Breaking it down by segment, the international business was the clear bright spot. International organic revenue growth accelerated to eight percent, the strongest pace since the first quarter of twenty twenty-four. Revenue in North America food, EMEA, Latin America food, and Asia Pacific food all outperformed. The weak links were North America beverages and international beverages, both of which missed expectations. Management was direct about it, saying the North America business performed below their expectations. So how do you frame this? Adam's bottom line is that this release probably clears the not-as-bad-as-feared bar. The third quarter itself was decent, and there are real signs of top-line progress, particularly internationally. But the full-year earnings cut is real and the North America margin story remains a headwind that the market will need to weigh. Net-net, this is a mixed print — better on sales, worse on the earnings trajectory. Watch how the stock reacts at the open as a read on how much of the bad news was already priced in.
